title: Deleting a gym also deletes its proof that it accepted the terms and the data agreement
what: The record of who accepted the terms, when and which version is described as kept for ever, but when MettleUp deletes a gym at its request, that record is deleted with it. HQ's own records survive the delete; this one does not. In a business with several branches, the acceptance is stored on one branch only, so deleting that branch also leaves the other branches with no acceptance, and their owners are asked again.
expected: The acceptance record outlives the gym, like HQ's own legal records, so MettleUp can still show what the gym agreed to after it leaves; and a branch delete never removes the business's acceptance.
who: MettleUp (legal record), owners of branch businesses
fix_line: Keep the acceptance rows when a gym is deleted, as HQ's own records are kept, and count a deleted branch's acceptance for the rest of the business

title: Records taken back by Undo this import stay on our server in full, for ever
what: When an owner undoes a wrong data import, the members, plans, memberships and receipts it made are only marked as removed: every name, mobile and amount stays on the server. Taken-back check-ins and expenses are the same. The nightly clean-up never clears them, so a wrong file (even another gym's list) stays stored with no end date.
expected: Records taken back are emptied of personal details after a short time, and the nightly clean-up clears them.
who: members of gyms that undo an import
fix_line: Have the nightly clean-up empty the details of records removed more than a set time ago

title: If the nightly clean-up stops, nobody is told, and the log-deletion promises quietly break
what: The nightly clean-up deletes the sign-in log after 7 days and creator addresses after a year, as the privacy notice says. If it fails, the only trace is a hidden server log line. The HQ system page shows no 'last clean-up' time, so a broken key or job could leave logs kept far longer than promised without anyone noticing.
expected: HQ shows when the clean-up last ran, and warns you when it has not run for a day or more.
who: you (MettleUp), and every gym's staff whose sign-in log is kept
fix_line: Show the last clean-up time in HQ and warn when it is more than a day old

title: After every branch of a business is deleted, the business's name stays on our server
what: A business with branches has its own row holding the business name. Deleting a gym removes the branch but leaves that row; when the last branch goes, the name stays with nothing pointing to it, and the delete's own check that nothing was left behind does not look at it.
expected: Deleting the last branch also deletes the business row.
who: owners of branch businesses that leave
how_often: every full offboarding of a branch business
fix_line: Remove the business row when its last branch is deleted
